the-extension-register-is-shown-to-every.why: THE GATE ON THE REGISTER, REMOVED. It is the notice's own ANY-OF — holders of any of the three retention acts see the notice, and the same three see what was extended — and with the condition gone a Sales Officer who holds none of them is shown a section listing which of the office's records had their retention extended, on which legal basis, citing which hold. That is the frontend directive's most explicit rule broken (a control a role cannot use does not exist on their screen), and it is also a disclosure: the extension register names holds and the disputes behind them. `retention-disposal.spec.ts` fails on the test named for a reader holding none of the three acts, which asserts the section's ABSENCE anchored on the refusal alert from the same render — without that anchor the absence would be satisfied by a page that had not hydrated, and `toHaveCount(0)` passes on its first poll. The anchor is why this plant can be caught at all.

the-basis-list-is-restated-on-the-screen.why: THE EXACT STATE OWNER DECISION 43 REMOVED — the screen carrying its own copy of a closed vocabulary the server already answers for. `GET /retention-archive/bases` exists so that *"the screen renders them rather than restating them"* (its controller's own words) and had NO CALLER AT ALL while this hardcoded pair sat here. Two homes for one closed fact is the defect this codebase refuses everywhere else, and the cost is specific rather than stylistic: a third basis added server-side would be unselectable, so a capability the server had granted would not exist on the screen. `retention-disposal.spec.ts` fails on the test that offers THREE bases from the mock and expects three options — the plant renders two. Note what the plant does NOT break: the existing 7c test asserts exactly the real closed two, so it passes either way, which is why the third-basis test had to be written rather than relying on it.

the-register-forgets-who-extended.why: THE ACTOR'S NAME DROPPED AT THE API, WHICH IS THE LAYER THE SCREEN CANNOT CHECK. `apps/web/lib/pdpl/retention-disposal-api.ts` declares this shape BY HAND over HTTP and TypeScript cannot compare it to the api's own view — which is exactly how the customer-import result panel broke, and why a field a screen reads is asserted on the RESPONSE BODY. The field stays present and typed, so nothing fails to compile and no Playwright mock notices: a mock supplies the name itself. EXACTLY ONE TEST DIES, AND THAT IS THE POINT RATHER THAN A SHORTFALL. `retention-disposal.e2e-spec.ts` fails with `expected null to be 'Retention E2E User'` on the wire assertion. **CORRECTED FROM THE MEASUREMENT: this `why` first claimed the Playwright register test dies too. IT DOES NOT, and could not** — that test MOCKS `/retention-notices/register` and supplies `extendedByName` itself, so the api service is not in its path at all. Measured with the plant live: 1 of 15 api e2e tests failed and the Playwright spec stayed 18/18. A mocked endpoint cannot refuse you, and it cannot drop a field either; the wire assertion is the only thing between this view and a screen reading `undefined`. I asserted a second test's behaviour without running it, which is the defect this repository keeps paying for, in the one file whose whole job is to say what each plant kills. REPOINTED 2026-10-23 (batch seven item 1): the projection moved onto owner decision 48's resolver, so the anchor it named no longer exists. `plant --self-test` refused it the moment the line changed — the EIGHTH time that mechanism has caught its own evidence expiring. Repointed at the new line rather than deleted: the hazard is unchanged, only the expression of it.
